title: Granular Route Economics Studio — Demo with Lyra Systems
summary: Studio-focused demo showing per-route telemetry, cost decomposition, and how Redwood's Console + Optimize suggestions reduce per-token spend. Customer asked about dedicated vs hosted, VPC/KMS needs, and how to map routes to chargeback; agreed to run a 2-week pilot with benchmarks and share security pack.
next_steps: Share pilot onboarding checklist and security pack (Redwood)
Provision trial org and sample route dataset (Lyra)
Follow-up call to review pilot results in 2 weeks (schedule)
action_items: Jamie Carter | Send security pack & pilot onboarding doc | due: 2026-04-17
Priya Natarajan | Setup trial org + seed sample routes for Lyra | due: 2026-04-20
Dev Patel | Provide example traffic slice and SLOs | due: 2026-04-16
Sofia Lim | Share cost allocation rules and billing contact | due: 2026-04-18
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 49m
Attendees: Jamie Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Tom Huang (Redwood Solutions); Marta Reyes (Lyra Head of ML), Dev Patel (Lyra SRE), Sofia Lim (Lyra FinOps), Evan Cho (Procurement)

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a sec. I'm Jamie Carter, i'm the AE for the account, with Priya our systems engineer. today we're going to run through what we call the "studio" demo focused on route-level economics and per-route dashboards, and then show some Optimize suggestions for lowering unit cost. does that line up with what you were hoping for?

[00:18] Marta: yeah thanks, Jamie. big picture for us is we want to get better visibility into how different product routes (like chat, summarization, and embed pipelines) are costing us. we currently have a pretty opaque bill from our provider and our finance team struggles to map usage to product teams.

[00:34] Sofia: right, and for us in FinOps the ask is: how do we map token spend to our internal chargeback? we want to be able to show per-feature cost, not just account-level spend.

[00:47] Priya: perfect, that's exactly what the Console's usage studio is built for — per-route telemetry, attribution and configurable chargeback keys. we'll walk through a live demo using a seeded dataset so you can see the drill-downs. quick qualification: whats your current model hosting? self-hosted endpoints or using a managed provider?

[01:05] Dev: currently we run a mix — some outbound customer chats hit OpenAI, some batch embeddings on our own infra, and we have a small private inference cluster for sensitive flows. latency SLOs vary by route; chat needs sub-300ms tail.

[01:22] Jamie: ok good, that mix is common. quick follow ups: do you need VPC / private control plane for regulatory reasons? and how strict are key management rules — KMS, HSM?

[01:34] Marta: yes, for certain PHI-adjacent features we need a VPC and KMS. we also need audit logs and SSO/SAML.

[01:42] Priya: noted. Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem and can integrate with customer KMS; audit logs and SSO are standard in the enterprise package — we'll include the SOC2 and architecture doc in the security pack.

[01:56] Tom: quick note on expectations: the demo will show Console insights + Optimize suggestions. Optimize will recommend batching sizes, caching prefixes and quantization tiers which, in tests, reduced per-token cost by 20-60% depending on route.

[02:10] Marta: that number is huge, curious on the caveats — does it impact quality, latency, or model parity?

[02:18] Priya: good question. for each suggestion Optimize includes an expected delta for latency and quality and flags suggestions that require quality validation. e.g., using 8-bit quantization on some open LLMs might slightly change output distributions; we run regression evals on your prompt suite during the pilot.

[02:36] --- demo starts ---

[02:39] [03:05] Priya: ok i'm sharing my screen — this is the Console studio homepage, you can see an overview of total tokens, active routes and a sparkline of median latency. on the left is our route catalog. i'll open the 'Customer Chat' route.

[03:22] [03:40] Priya: here you have a route timeline, tokens-in and tokens-out, and importantly the cost decomposition panel: model compute, GPU time, caching savings and egress. note the route tags — product:chat, env:prod, team:customer — those tags drive chargeback.

[03:58] Marta: those tags are nice. can we map to our internal cost centers? like product_id and business_unit?

[04:06] Priya: yes you can configure custom route keys and map them to chargeback export. CSV or our billing API includes per-route breakdown with your custom keys.

[04:18] [04:40] Jamie: can you show the rate-limited tail breakdown? we often want to see 95/99th latency by route during spikes.

[04:45] [05:05] Priya: sure — switching panel — here's a latency histogram and tail latency slider. you can overlay model variants so you can see how gpt-like models compare to smaller distilled models. note that the console's comparison is sampled and annotated with the sampling rate.

[05:20] Dev: sampling — does that mean the console doesn't have per-request logs for everything? we need trace-level for debugging incidents.

[05:30] Priya: we store traces for requests up to your retention window; sampling is for analytics panels to reduce storage and compute. full request logs are available via the audit and trace export if you enable that and increase retention.

[05:44] [06:10] Priya: switching to the cost-playbook tab — here Optimize lists active recommendations for this route. for example, it suggests a batching window of 40ms for the chat route which reduces GPU context-switch overhead. it also suggests prefix caching for repeated prompts (they call it KV cache in some docs — sometimes transcripts read it as KV cash, sorry for the joke).

[06:29] Marta: prefix caching seems dangerous for dynamic prompts, does it change responses?

[06:35] Priya: only when prefixes are stable and deterministic. Optimize flags risky caches and will only enable them for routes you sign off on. there's a safety toggle and we run A/B tests through the rollout engine.

[06:50] [07:10] Priya: here's the per-token cost heatmap, you can filter by model family and time-of-day. you can see that late-night batch embeddings are the biggest cost center per request but low in percent of total traffic.

[07:25] Sofia: can we export that to our finance stack? like our chargeback tool?

[07:30] Priya: yes, export options: CSV, S3 export, or direct connector to common FinOps tools. the export includes mapping keys so you don't have to do manual joins.

[07:40] [08:05] Jamie: let's talk about dedicated vs hosted — Lyra, you mentioned some privacy sensitive flows. do you have an estimate of peak QPS for those flows?

[08:12] Dev: peak for chat is ~120 QPS during rush. embeddings batch jobs run overnight at ~600 concurrent jobs but low QPS.

[08:22] Jamie: for that profile Dedicated makes sense for predictable throughput and isolation; Hosted is great for fast onboarding and lower ops. a hybrid approach is common: sensitive routes on private/dedicated, non-sensitive on hosted with routing policies.

[08:36] Marta: how seamless is routing? can we have automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated is saturated?

[08:43] Priya: yes, Smart Routing can failover automatically and we support model variant fallbacks. policies are configurable per-route with thresholds and can be simulated in the Console before you deploy.

[08:55] [09:20] Dev: curious about model pinning and rollouts — how do we test a new model without impacting prod?

[09:28] Priya: Rollouts support canary percentages, A/B tests and automatic rollback on quality regressions. rollouts are model-version aware so you can pin a route to a specific model version.

[09:38] [10:05] Priya: i'll click into the Optimize suggestion detail — this one shows expected cost savings: 28% reduction in tokens/sec cost, expected latency +18ms. there's a confidence score and linked eval results. clicking the eval shows sample prompts and diff highlights.

[10:26] Marta: if we push a suggestion, is there an audit trail? we need approvals recorded for compliance.

[10:33] Priya: yes every change goes into the audit log with user, timestamp, and delta. we'll include an example audit log export in the security pack.

[10:45] [11:12] Tom: quick live experiment — i'm going to enable a simulated batching change for a test route. this is non-prod demo data. you'll see the simulated cost delta and latency projection.

[11:20] [12:05] Priya: simulation done — console shows projected 23% cost delta and a 12ms median increase. note the regression check flagged two prompts as potential quality drift; you can open them to review.

[12:28] Marta: those flagged prompts look like our legal disclaimers — we can't have hallucinations there. what's the rollback policy?

[12:36] Priya: automatic rollback on quality regression is supported. you can also gate changes on manual sign-off by a list of approvers — the approval workflow integrates with SSO groups.

[12:50] [13:15] Dev: network questions — if we run private deployment do we manage the infra entirely? how does Redwood's private control plane interact with our VPC?

[13:24] Priya: in Private mode you run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, Redwood provides the orchestration agent. we support private networking, peering, and local KMS or HSM. full topology and runbook will be in the architecture doc.

[13:40] Evan: procurement question — what's the typical contract length for Dedicated and Private?

[13:46] Jamie: Dedicated is often reserved capacity monthly or annual commits; Private is an enterprise license plus support. we'll send a pricing/contract template; we can structure a pilot with limited term.

[14:00] [14:30] Priya: back to the console — here's the chargeback export UI. you map route keys to your internal ledger codes. once mapped, you can auto-generate billing rows.

[14:45] Sofia: do you support tagging via headers so our app can push product_id?

[14:52] Priya: yup, route-level metadata can be pushed in the request header or mapped from tokenized routing. we've seen teams use either approach.

[15:05] [15:35] Jamie: ok let's talk about the pilot scope — we typically run a 2-week pilot that seeds traffic or uses replayed traces and runs Optimize suggestions and evals. does that sound reasonable?

[15:48] Marta: yes, 2 weeks is fine. our SRE will provide traces and we can route a small % of prod to the trial.

[15:58] Dev: is there cost to run the pilot? and will it appear on our bill?

[16:05] Jamie: pilot pricing is negotiable; usually we provide trial credits for hosted usage and provide guidance for dedicated sizing. we'll include a pilot cost estimate in the follow-up.

[16:20] [16:40] Priya: one more thing — Optimize can recommend quantization tiers per-model. for example some models can go to int8 with negligible quality loss, others not. we surface a per-model recommendation and the regression delta for your prompt set.

[16:55] Marta: do you run those regressions on our real prompts or synthetic ones?

[17:01] Priya: on your prompt suite. for the pilot we'll ask you to hand over a representative prompt corpus and expected outputs for the critical routes.

[17:15] [17:40] Dev: about logs — what retention windows are typical? we can't keep full traces forever.

[17:47] Priya: default retention is 30 days for traces and 90 days for aggregated analytics; enterprise can extend retention. trace exports to your S3 are recommended for long-term archival.

[18:00] [18:22] Jamie: time check — we have about 30 minutes left, let's cover a few more questions and then do a short recap and next steps.

[18:33] [19:00] Marta: curious about cost attribution accuracy — what's the granularity? token-level? per-request?

[19:10] Priya: attribution is per-request with token-level granularity for compute cost; we also attribute fixed infrastructure overhead proportionally across routes based on configured rules. you can choose allocation rules in the chargeback settings.

[19:26] Sofia: our finance team wants the exact mapping logic documented so auditors can follow it.

[19:31] Priya: noted — we'll add a chargeback mapping appendix to the security pack with formulas and examples.

[19:45] [20:05] Dev: on fallback behavior during congestion — is there a way to degrade gracefully and still preserve SLAs for critical routes?

[20:12] Priya: yes, route policies support prioritized queues, graceful degradation (e.g., trim response length), and automated model fallback to cheaper low-latency variants. all policy changes can be simulated.

[20:30] [21:00] Jamie: quick callout — one common confusion is cost shown in Console vs invoice. Console shows blended and attributable costs; invoice is raw cloud/GPU charges. we provide reconciliation tools.

[21:17] Marta: good, reconciliation is important.

[21:25] [22:00] Priya: demo close — last panel: "pilot diagnostics" — here we'll run a smoke replay and show expected cost vs baseline. you can provision a sandbox org and replay traces.

[22:18] [22:45] Priya: ok switching back to camera — that's the end of the live walkthrough. open to questions.

[22:52] Marta: thanks — overall pretty compelling. couple concerns: 1) how invasive is the agent for on-prem? 2) how long to provision a dedicated pool?

[23:05] Priya: agent is lightweight and installs into your VPC; we can provide a reproducible terraform module. Dedicated pool typically takes a few days for reserved infra provisioning in our regions, plus config. we'll include a provisioning timeline in the follow-up.

[23:20] Evan: procurement will want an SLA example and liability terms.

[23:27] Jamie: we'll attach a sample SLA and contract template.

[23:35] [24:00] Marta: last product question — can we test Optimize suggestions in a canary where only a small percentage of traffic uses them?

[24:06] Priya: yes canary rollouts supported; you can run A/B and automatic rollback on regression thresholds.

[24:20] [25:00] Jamie: ok recap / next steps: we'll send the security pack (SOC2, architecture, audit export examples), pricing and pilot estimate, and the pilot onboarding doc. Lyra will send representative traces and the prompt corpus. Priya will set up a trial org and seed sample routes.

[25:30] Sofia: sounds good, please cc our finance contact on the pricing.

[25:40] Jamie: noted. any blockers on scheduling the pilot kickoff next Monday?

[25:47] Marta: next Monday is fine.

[25:52] [26:10] Jamie: great thank you all, we'll follow up by end of day with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot.

[26:20] [26:40] Priya: thanks everyone, happy to dive deeper into the private deployment runbook in the next call.

[26:50] Marta: thanks, bye.

[27:00] End of recording (note: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and ASR artifacts like 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', and minor speaker attribution differences).
